3. While entertaining the instant writ petition on 07.11.2024, this Court had accorded interim relief to the petitioners.

For ready reference the order dated 07.11.2024 is reproduced hereunder:-
"1. Heard Shri K.M. Tripathi, learned counsel for the petitioners and Shri G.P. Singh,
learned A.G.A.-I for the State respondents.
2.

The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 12.07.2021 registered as Case Crime No.1468 of 2021 under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sahibabad, District Ghaziabad.
Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioners in the aforesaid case.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that mutual divorce proceeding had been carried out between the parties, wherein, a sum of Rs.18,75,000/- was settled as full and final amount to be paid by petitioner to the victim.
The said amount was to be paid in three installment.

Out of which two installments have been paid by petitioners and final installments is to be paid at the time of quashing the FIR, which is reflected from the order dated 23.07.2024 passed by Principal Judge, Family Court, North-West, Rohini, Delhi in HMA Petition No.1874 of 2024 (Sarabjeet Singh vs. Smt. Aparna).

In this backdrop, he submits that once the parties have already moved an application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 and the same has already been adjudicated/decreed by the Competent Court, the impugned proceeding is per-se unsustainable and the same is liable to be quashed.

In support of his submission, he has placed reliance on the judgements of Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2003(4) SCC 675, Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of investigation and another J.T. 2008(9) SC 192, Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012)
10 SCC 303, Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand (2014) 9 SCC 653 and also in Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466.

4. Today, when the matter is taken up, learned counsel for the petitioners have placed a demand draft of Rs.6,75,000/-(No.860414 dated 27.11.2024) towards final settlement, which took place between the parties on 29.09.2024 in HMA - 448/21, Divorce Suit (Sarabjeet v. Aparna Sachdeva)
before learned Judge Family Court, North/West: Rohini: Delhi.

The paragraph no.5 of said settlement, which is relevant is reproduced hereunder:-
"It is further agreed between the parties that the Husband shall pay Rs.6,75,000 (Six Lakhs Seventy Five Thousand only) to the wife at the time of Quashing of FIR No.1468/21 PS - Sahibabad, U/S 498A/323/504/506 IPC and U/S 3 and 4 Dowry Prohition Act in Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad (UP), within one month after second motion and wife shall cooperate and sign all necessary documents."

5. In this backdrop, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in terms of said settlement the demand draft of Rs.6,75,000/- is being handed over to the wife, therefore, the FIR may be quashed.

6. Learned AGA fairly states that as there is matrimonial dispute and the parties have already settled the said dispute amicably before the Family Court, North/West: Rohini: Delhi, he has no objection,
in case the FIR is quashed.
Similar view has been taken by learned counsel for the informant.

7. Considering the factual situation, as the dispute has come to be amicably resolved under the settlement agreement dated 29.09.2024, before the Family Court, North/West: Rohini: Delhi,
therefore, pending proceedings would serve no purpose and the same are liable to be quashed in the light of the judgements of the Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana and others, 2003(4) SCC 675 and Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, 2012(10) SCC 303.

Reliance has also been placed on the judgment of Division Bench of this Court dated 16.9.2022 in Criminal Misc.
Writ Petition No.8510 of 2022 (Anuj Pandey v. State of U.P. & Ors.) wherein it is observed that the High Court has ample power under its inherent jurisdiction to quash the first information report in which the parties have settled their disputes which are of private in nature and have no any grave impact on the society.

sentences.text: The time of courts as well as investigating agencies are very precious which should not be wasted in any futile proceedings where the chance of conviction is bleak.

8. Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh (supra) has held in para-61 that;
"the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences Under Section 320 of the Code.

Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

sentences.text: power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.

Similarly, any compromise between the victim and offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.

But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil favour stand on different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile,
civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.

In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

9. Since the dispute between the parties have already been settled amicably vide settlement agreement dated 29.09.2024, pending proceedings would serve no purpose and the same are liable to be quashed in the light of the aforesaid judgments.
10.

The writ petition is allowed and theF.I.R. dated 12.07.2021 registered as Case Crime No.1468 of 2021 under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sahibabad, District Ghaziabad is hereby quashed.
